manualReview.summary: The published maternal effects do not establish the sex-adjusted contrast within saline
manualReview.note: Rodriguez-Zas et al. studied individual hypothalamic libraries from 112 day-60 pigs. Maternal exposure was assigned to gilts. The authors report trimmed-mean normalization and edgeR 3.14 for the maternal exposure, juvenile treatment and sex factors and their interactions. The September 5 manual review records retrieval of the original Illinois DOCX and cites continued-sources/advancement-sources-b-2026-09-05/GSE245146/scope-audit.json. The November review independently checked all 30 pages rendered by the Illinois-linked viewer. Table S1 gives gene symbols, log2 fold changes and FDR for 159 selected maternal main-effect rows. The maternal column and paper methods give the direction as control minus PRRSV. The S1 caption gives the reverse order. The authors do not supply the coding and weights needed to identify this coefficient with the common maternal effect within saline. Tables S2 and S3 give pathway enrichment. Figure 5 shows control minus maternal immune activation for pain-pathway genes separately in saline-treated males and females. HypoExplorer uses 17 maternal-PRRSV and 21 maternal-control saline offspring. Its additive limma model on log2(TPM + 1) estimates a common PRRSV-minus-control coefficient with sex as a covariate. The pig is the observation and the model has no litter term. GEO provides sample expression values. The reviewed sources did not yield an author gene table or fitted contrast for this coefficient. Author effect concordance, raw P values and FDR for the registered contrast remain unassessed. See data/author-validation/continued-sources/GSE245146/codex-2026-11-24/SEARCH_LOG.md.

verificationReview.reason: The authors analyzed saline, fasting and poly(I:C) offspring of both sexes. Table S1 labels the maternal coefficient as a main effect in that analysis. Its precise reference cells or averaging weights are undocumented. Figure 5 conditions each maternal comparison on sex and juvenile treatment. Neither source supplies an identifiable reference for the single sex-adjusted maternal coefficient in the 38 registered saline libraries.
verificationReview.nextStep: Reopen on a gene-level author table or original fitted contrast that identifies the day-60 saline cohort and the common maternal effect adjusted for sex. Either contrast direction is usable when documented. Orient author effects to PRRSV minus control before comparison. For a fitted model, verify the sample identities, biological unit, design and contrast weights. Assess the available identifiers, effect units, coverage and any reported P values or FDR.
